approach:
# Attempt ATT-0002 — Extend CKgP/gonality geometry to M_5,8

## Selected case and goal

RED-0001 reduces the degree-16 pure-Tate problem for Mbar_g,n to finitely many open pure-weight inputs, one of which is the pure-weight piece of the open stack M_5,8. The published low-homology induction (SRC-0002, (6.1) and proof of Theorem 1.5(3)) needs, for even k=16 and n>=2, open base cases whenever 16 >= 2g-2+n. For (g,n)=(5,8) one has 2g-2+n=16, so M_5,8 is exactly on the threshold and is mandatory.

Published CKgP range (SRC-0002 Table 1; SRC-0004 Lemma 10.13): c(5)=7, so M_5,n has CKgP and A^*=R^* only for n<=7. The missing pointed case is therefore precisely n=8.

Goal of this single approach: extend the gonality/CKgP geometry of SRC-0004 from n<=7 to n=8, and record what is proved versus what remains open. We do **not** claim that CONJ-0001 or the full RED-0001 list is settled.

## Strategy (gonality stratification)

Filter M_5,8 by gonality:

  M^2_5,8 subset M^3_5,8 subset M_5,8,

where M^k_g,n is the locus of curves admitting a degree-<=k map to P^1. For g=5 the Brill–Noether maximum gonality is 4, so the open complement of the trigonal locus is the open tetragonal stratum.

By the standard CKgP lemmas (SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2 / SRC-0004 Lemmas 3.2–3.4, 3.10): CKgP of a space follows from CKgP of the strata in a finite stratification, and proper surjective images of CKgP stacks again have CKgP. Tautological support of classes on a closed locus reduces to tautological pushforwards from the successive differences.

### Step A — Hyperelliptic and trigonal loci (settled)

SRC-0004 Lemma 9.9: for g>=4 and n<=g+7, the locus M^3_g,n has CKgP and every Chow class supported on it is tautological on M_g,n. Here g=5 and n=8<=12, so M^3_5,8 is covered completely by the published argument (hyperelliptic included via the n<=2g+6 range of Theorem 6.1 / 6.2).

**Claim A (source-verified).** M^3_5,8 has CKgP, and classes supported on M^3_5,8 are tautological.

### Step B — Reduction of the open tetragonal stratum

Let H_4,5,8 be the Hurwitz stack of degree-4 covers of P^1 by smooth genus-5 curves with 8 marked points, and let beta: H_4,5,8 -> M_5,8 be the forgetful map. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.9 identifies

  H^4_4,5,n := H'_4,5,n minus Supp R^1 pi_* F(3)  =  H_4,5,n \ beta^{-1}(M^3_5,n)

for the Casnati–Ekedahl open with f_1 >= 4. In particular, the restricted map

  beta' : H^4_4,5,8 -> M_5,8 \ M^3_5,8

is proper and surjective. Hence CKgP for H^4_4,5,8 implies CKgP for the open tetragonal stratum (SRC-0004 Lemma 3.10 / SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2(2)). Moreover, if every class on H^4_4,5,8 in the image of A^*((PE^vee)^8) pushes forward to a tautological class, then A^*=R^* on the open tetragonal stratum follows as in Lemma 10.13.

### Step C — Where the n<=7 argument stops

The n<=7 proof (Lemma 10.13) uses the evaluation map (10.9) for the rank-2 bundle W = O_PE(2) tensor gamma^* F^vee. SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6 guarantees surjectivity of evaluation on n distinct points on a smooth complete-intersection curve whenever n <= 4 f_1 - 2g + 1. For the balanced open f_1 >= 4 and g=5 this bound is

  4f - 2g + 1 = 4*4 - 10 + 1 = 7.

At n=8 the numerical criterion fails by exactly one. Explicitly, for the balanced splitting F=(4,4) and n=8, the Serre-dual degree appearing in the proof of Lemma 10.6 is

  deg(omega_C tensor W_{f_i}^vee (Gamma)) = 4 f_i + n - 2g - 14 = 16 + 8 - 10 - 14 = 0

for each summand i=1,2. Thus H^1(C, W(-Gamma)) need not vanish: evaluation may drop rank precisely when at least one of these degree-0 line bundles is effective (equivalently, trivial as a degree-0 bundle with a section).

Consequently the vector-bundle tower (10.10)

  H^f_4,g,n  subset  Y|_U  -> U  subset (PE^vee)^n  -> B

— which supplies CKgP for n<=7 via Lemmas 10.11–10.12 — does **not** automatically contain the image of H^4_4,5,8 when n=8.

### Step D — Proposed repair: split by evaluation rank

Write H^4_4,5,8 = H_U sqcup H_D, where:

- **H_U** is the open locus of covers for which the eight marked points impose independent conditions on H^0(PE^vee, W) (i.e., land in the open U of surjective evaluation);
- **H_D** is the closed degeneracy locus where evaluation fails.

On H_U the same tower as (10.10) applies with n=8: H_U sits openly in a vector-bundle kernel over an open of (PE^vee)^8, and B has CKgP (quotient of an open in affine space by products of GL and SL_2). Therefore:

**Claim D1 (proved from published lemmas).** H_U has CKgP. Its image in M_5,8 \ M^3_5,8 has CKgP. Classes on that image coming from A^*((PE^vee)^8) push forward to tautological classes by SRC-0004 Lemma 10.5 / Proposition 8.4 (FPH / ramification generators).

What remains is H_D.

### Step E — Geometry of the degeneracy locus (not completed)

For F=(4,4) and n=8, failure of evaluation means that for at least one i in {1,2},

  H^0(C, omega_C tensor W_{f_i}^vee (p_1+...+p_8)) != 0,

with the line bundle of degree 0. Geometrically, the eight points are residual to a special divisor class on the Casnati–Ekedahl model PE^vee (a P^2-bundle over P^1). A complete treatment would require:

1. identifying irreducible components of H_D (expected: loci where a residual linear series forces the cover into a more special Casnati–Ekedahl splitting, or forces a relation among the eight markings);
2. proving each component has CKgP (e.g., by exhibiting it as an open in a tower of projective/Grassmann/affine bundles, or as a proper image of a previously settled stack);
3. proving that Chow classes supported on each component push forward to tautological classes on M_5,8.

None of (1)–(3) is carried out in the supplied sources for (g,n)=(5,8).

### Step F — Link to pure-weight Tate (what CKgP would give)

SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3: if a smooth open X in a smooth proper DM stack has CKgP, then cl: A^*(X) -> oplus_k W_k H^k(X) is surjective. In particular, for even k, W_k H^k(X) is pure Hodge–Tate (algebraic of Tate type). Applied to X=M_5,8, CKgP would imply

  W_16 H^16(M_5,8) = RH^16(M_5,8)  subset  oplus Q(-8)

(and dually the pure-weight BM quotient W_{-16} H^{BM}_16(M_5,8) is a sum of Q(8)). Combined with the boundary exact sequence (6.1) and the already-known even cohomology through degree 14 (THM-0002), this would discharge the M_5,8 pure-weight input in RED-0001.

**However:** pure Tate is weaker than full CKgP / A^*=R^*. Even a proof that only W_16 H^16(M_5,8) is algebraic would suffice for the degree-16 induction at this base case. The present attempt does not establish that weaker statement either, because the contribution of H_D to pure weight 16 is uncontrolled.

### Step G — What this does not claim

- Does not claim CKgP for M_5,8.
- Does not claim W_16 H^16(M_5,8) is pure Tate.
- Does not finish RED-0001: the cases M_3,12, M_6,6, M_7,4, M_8,n (n=0,1,2) remain.
- Does not upgrade an arithmetic prediction, a semisimplification, or an unproved tautological pairing to a proof.
- Does not replace the stack by its coarse space (CKgP statements are for the stack; cf. SRC-0004 Lemma 3.9).

## Summary of progress

The missing case M_5,8 reduces, via published gonality and Hurwitz geometry, to a single geometric residual: the evaluation-degeneracy locus H_D inside the balanced tetragonal Hurwitz stack H^4_4,5,8. The complementary open H_U is under full control by the same vector-bundle / FPH methods that give n<=7. Completing either CKgP or the weaker pure-weight Tate statement for M_5,8 requires a new analysis of H_D that is not present in the supplied corpus.
assumptions: Rational coefficients Q throughout; stacks over characteristic 0 (or >5 as in SRC-0004).
Maximal gonality of a smooth genus-5 curve is 4, so M_5,8 is the union of the trigonal closed locus and the open tetragonal stratum.
Standard CKgP permanence under open immersions, finite stratifications, affine/Grassmann bundles, and proper surjective DM morphisms (SRC-0002 Prop. 4.2; SRC-0004 Section 3).
Casnati-Ekedahl structure for degree-4 covers as used in SRC-0004 Sections 8-10.
Boundary right-exact sequence (SRC-0002 (6.1)) relating H_k(Mbar) to the pure-weight BM quotient of the open moduli stack.
claims: For the degree-16 low-homology induction, (g,n)=(5,8) is a mandatory open base case because 16 = 2g-2+n.
Published range: M_5,n has CKgP and A^*=R^* for all n<=c(5)=7 (SRC-0002 Table 1; SRC-0004 Lemma 10.13), so n=8 is the first missing pointed case in genus 5.
By SRC-0004 Lemma 9.9, M^3_5,8 has CKgP and classes supported on it are tautological (since 8 <= g+7 = 12).
The open tetragonal stratum M_5,8 \ M^3_5,8 is the proper surjective image of H^4_4,5,8 (SRC-0004 Lemma 10.9).
The n<=7 CKgP proof for the tetragonal open uses surjectivity of evaluation for W on n points, which is guaranteed only for n <= 4f_1-2g+1 = 7 when f_1>=4 and g=5 (SRC-0004 Lemma 10.6).
At n=8 and F=(4,4), the Serre-dual degrees in the evaluation criterion are exactly 0, so evaluation may fail; the published vector-bundle tower (10.10) does not automatically cover all of H^4_4,5,8.
On the open H_U where evaluation remains surjective, the tower (10.10) still applies: H_U has CKgP, and image classes from A^*((PE^vee)^8) push forward tautologically (Lemmas 10.5, 10.11, 10.12).

If M_5,8 had CKgP, then SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3 would force W_16 H^16(M_5,8) to be algebraic pure Hodge-Tate (a sum of Q(-8)), discharging this RED-0001 input; this implication is not a proof that CKgP holds.
The residual degeneracy locus H_D is not classified, not shown to have CKgP, and not shown to contribute only tautological or pure-Tate classes in weight 16.
gap_markers: GAP-1 (critical): No source-verified irreducible decomposition of the evaluation-degeneracy locus H_D subset H^4_4,5,8 for F=(4,4) and n=8.
GAP-2 (critical): CKgP is not proved for any component of H_D.
GAP-3 (critical): Tautological pushforward of classes supported on H_D to M_5,8 \ M^3_5,8 is not proved.
GAP-4: Even the weaker pure-weight statement W_16 H^16(M_5,8) = RH^16(M_5,8) (or pure Tate without full A^*=R^*) is not proved, because the H_D contribution in weight 16 is uncontrolled.
GAP-5: Extending CKgP to M_5,8 would not finish RED-0001; remaining obstruction cases are M_3,12, M_6,6, M_7,4, and M_8,n for n=0,1,2.
GAP-6: No claim is made from Chenevier-Lannes arithmetic predictions, from semisimplifications of Galois representations, or from any tautological pairing whose perfectness was not proved.

GAP-7: Scope trap check — all statements are about the moduli stack M_5,8 (not its coarse space); Poincare duality / BM pure-weight shifts are tracked only conditionally on CKgP via SRC-0002 Lemma 4.3 and (6.1).
